targets.from: judgement values, no photographs measured: a low, dense, rounded dune mound wider than tall (Santa Barbara Botanic Garden listing: about 0.3-0.9 m high by 0.6-1.2 m wide)

young.note: a small dense tuft on open sand

decadent.note: an old mound half buried in sand, grey dead stems among the green

description: A low, dense, heath-like shrub of the coastal dunes and sandy bluffs, its upright stems crowded with tiny needle-like leaves in tufts. From late summer into fall it is covered with small golden-yellow flower heads.

season_notes.winter: Dark green tufts on the grey dunes, last fall's flower heads brown and fluffy.
season_notes.spring: New growth freshens the green and the stems lengthen.
season_notes.summer: Buds gather at the branch tips and the first yellow heads open in August.
season_notes.fall: The mounds glow golden with flowers, alive with late bees and butterflies.

range.where: coastal dunes, sandy bluffs and coastal sage scrub from the northern Bay Area (San Francisco's dune remnants) south to the Los Angeles area

notes: Grown from chamise for the many stems and the fascicled needle-leaf foliage (leaves about 1 cm, in comb-like fans, Wikipedia), but as a low, rounded, leafy-to-the-ground mound rather than chamise's tall open vase, and in a slightly brighter green. The wand tips (foliage.tips, as chamise) carry the season: golden yellow in fall when it flowers (Calscape: summer and fall), brown seed heads in winter. Doubts: no source read gave a firm height (Wikipedia: rarely near 1 m; nursery and Calscape listings 0.3-1.2 m), and no source read named animals that eat it, so eaten_by is empty; it gives cover to brush rabbits and quail on the dunes and nectar to insects, and white-crowned sparrows forage around it (not in the animal library). The Jepson eFlora page would not load (a verification wall), so Jepson is not cited.
